title: Unraveling the mitochondrial gene rearrangements and structural plasticity of Tanytarsini (Diptera: Chironomidae)
content:
Abstract
Mitochondrial gene order is generally conserved in insects, serving as a reliable marker for tracing evolutionary history. However, the mechanisms driving sporadic structural variations remain poorly understood, particularly in hyper-diverse lineages like Tanytarsini Zavřel 1917 (Diptera: Chironomidae). Here, we generated 66 new mitogenomes, extending mitogenomic coverage to 10 previously unsequenced genera. Our analyses reveal a distinct pocket of mitogenomic instability within the Micropsectra-group, where we identify rare gene rearrangements. Comparative reconstruction suggests that these lineage-specific patterns most likely originated from a single ancestral tandem duplication spanning the COII-ND3 region, followed by differential random loss. The observed relaxation of purifying selection and a highly distinctive Cys to Ser substitution underscore the evolutionary plasticity of this rearranged region. Furthermore, we report that the marine species Pontomyia natans Edwards 1926 possesses the longest mitogenome currently published in Diptera, driven by the expansion of intergenic spacers. Our phylogenetic analyses corroborate morphological inference regarding the Micropsectra-group’s position, addressing topological uncertainties observed in previous fragment-based studies. Collectively, these findings establish the first documented case of large-scale mitogenomic rearrangement in Chironomidae, highlighting a potential link between ecological constraints and mitogenomic structural diversity.
